record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Find new proofs that the end-to-end distance of the four-dimensional self-avoiding walk has exponent 1/2 with logarithmic corrections.

evidence.quote: d = 4 Self avoiding walk: find new proofs that the end-to-end distance has an exponent of 1/2 with log corrections.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the simple (strictly) self-avoiding walk on the four-dimensional integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^4$: for each integer $n \ge 0$, let $c_n$ denote the number of nearest-neighbor walks $\omega = (\omega_0, \omega_1, \dots, \omega_n)$ in $\mathbb{Z}^4$ with $\omega_0 = 0$, $|\omega_{i+1} - \omega_i| = 1$, and $\omega_i \ne \omega_j$ for all $0 \le i < j \le n$. Let $\mathbb{E}_n$ denote the expectation with respect to the uniform probability measure on the set of such $n$-step self-avoiding walks, and define the mean-square end-to-end distance
$$\langle |\omega_n|^2 \rangle_n \;=\; \mathbb{E}_n\bigl[|\omega_n|^2\bigr].$$

It is conjectured that there exists a constant $C > 0$ such that, as $n \to \infty$,
$$\langle |\omega_n|^2 \rangle_n \;\sim\; C\, n\, (\log n)^{1/4},$$
that is, the end-to-end distance grows like $n^{1/2}$ with a logarithmic correction of power $1/8$.

Provide a rigorous proof of this asymptotic behavior, or more generally establish that the end-to-end distance exponent equals $1/2$ with an explicit logarithmic correction. New proofs, by any method (renormalization group analysis, supersymmetric field-theoretic representations, lace expansion variants, or otherwise), are sought for this critical-dimension result.
artifact.category_tag: Self-avoiding walks at the critical dimension
artifact.status_search_result: For the strictly self-avoiding walk in $d=4$, the conjectured $n^{1/2}(\log n)^{1/8}$ behavior of the end-to-end distance remains unproven. Rigorous renormalization-group results of Bauerschmidt, Brydges, and Slade established logarithmic corrections for related observables (susceptibility with exponent $1/4$ and finite-order correlation length) of the continuous-time weakly self-avoiding walk in four dimensions, but the end-to-end distance asymptotics — even for the weakly self-avoiding model, and certainly for the strictly self-avoiding model — has not been proven. The problem is widely regarded as open, and new proofs are explicitly sought.

status_evidence.title: Logarithmic Correction for the Susceptibility of the 4-Dimensional Weakly Self-Avoiding Walk
status_evidence.snippet: The susceptibility of the continuous-time weakly self-avoiding walk on Z^d in d=4 has a logarithmic correction to mean-field scaling with exponent 1/4.
status_evidence.claim: Logarithmic corrections proven for susceptibility (not end-to-end distance) of the weakly self-avoiding walk in d=4.

status_evidence.title: Finite-Order Correlation Length for Four-Dimensional Weakly Self-Avoiding Walk
status_evidence.snippet: The correlation length of order p has a logarithmic correction to mean-field scaling for the four-dimensional continuous-time weakly self-avoiding walk.
status_evidence.claim: Related logarithmic-correction results exist for the weakly self-avoiding walk but not for the end-to-end distance of the strict SAW.

status_evidence.title: On the existence of critical exponents for self-avoiding walks
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of critical exponents for self-avoiding walks, indicating that the d=4 case for the strict SAW remains conjectural.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of the conjectured end-to-end distance exponent with log corrections for the strict 4D SAW remains open.
